newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Germany will meet EMU deficit target.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Germany will meet EMU deficit target.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday Germany's 1997 government deficit would be below three percent of economic output, in line with the Maastricht guidelines for economic and monetary union, despite a report by an independent panel that it would be 3.3 percent.
Waigel said the report by the Council of Economic Advisers, also known as the "Five Wise Men", was an affirmation of government policies and an indictment of the opposition.
The panel called for drastic spending reductions and reform of the social welfare state.
"Fiscal policy has created the conditions that the state deficit in 1997 will fall below three percent of gross domestic product with an ample margin of safety," Waigel said in a statement.
Spending cuts agreed late Thursday in the parliamentary budget committee will help reach the goal, he said.
Waigel said the panel affirmed the government's policy of parallel cuts in taxes and spending, and "underscored the necessity of strict consolidation efforts."
The business sector's reluctance to invest, and the low level of foreign investment in Germany are warning signals that must be taken seriously, he said.
Economic recovery and stable prices will continue next year, but will not be enough to spark a marked improvement in the labour market, he said.
